question.worked_solution:
The given repeating decimal can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}3.\overset{―}{03} & =3.030\,303… \\  & =3+0.03+0.000\,3+0.000\,003+… \\  & ={{3+\frac{3}{100}+\frac{3}{10\,000}+\frac{3}{1\,000\,000}+⋯.}_{⏟}}_{\text{geometric series}}\end{aligned}
$$

We see that we have a geometric series where the first term is ${a}_{1}=3$ and the common ratio is $\frac{1}{100}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}3.\overset{―}{03} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }3{(\frac{1}{100})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }300(\frac{1}{100}){(\frac{1}{100})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }300{(\frac{1}{100})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$
